evidence.experimental_conditions: Sensitization: 2% methyl ester of pelargonic acid in acetone, 100 µL on dorsal skin; Challenge: 0.2% methyl ester of pelargonic acid in acetone, 50 µL in buccal mucosa; Species: SD rats (3 months old); Time: 48 h after last application
evidence.support_text: A study tested the tissue response of the methyl ester of pelargonic acid in rat buccal mucosa. Sensitization was with 2% solution on dorsal skin; challenge was with 0.2% and 2.0% solutions in buccal mucosa. Both concentrations caused increased cellularity, mainly mononuclear. The low concentration induced stronger inflammatory reactions than the high concentration for the methyl ester. The substance was said to have shown a sensitization tendency. Cellular infiltrates in the buccal mucosa were recorded.
